records.label: Iceland pre-industrial natural carrying capacity and population near 1300
pressure_evidence: Haraldsson and Olafsdottir construct a pre-industrial biological-production model and estimate sustainable Icelandic population at 40,000-80,000.
The Cambridge historical synthesis reports indirect population estimates of 40,000-60,000, a pre-modern maximum around 50,000-60,000, and repeated climate, famine, eruption, and animal-loss checks.
Iceland remained predominantly agricultural and animal-husbandry based; the carrying-capacity model is explicitly tied to local vegetation and livestock production rather than imported food.
shock_flags: AD 1300 volcanic eruption falls inside the interval
cool climate and episodic harvest/livestock failures
historical population estimates are indirect rather than an enumeration
records.food_regime: local pastoral agriculture, hay, dairy, meat, fishing, and limited trade
records.boundary_description: The Iceland island boundary, matching the complete EU5 Iceland area.
records.boundary_source: EU5 calibrated island geometry; historical island-wide population and capacity studies
records.source_family_independence: independent dynamic carrying-capacity model plus historical demographic synthesis
records.notes: The capacity interval is taken from the independent 2006 pre-industrial model, while the population interval comes from the historical synthesis. The record remains validation-only because no cited numeric local-calorie share is available and the literature contains a labor-scarcity interpretation that conflicts with a simple fixed Malthusian ceiling; the 1300 eruption is retained as uncertainty rather than silently removed.
